item.text:
Use the finitely supported coefficient representation. Identify
\[
R^{(I\sqcup J)}\cong R^{(I)}\oplus R^{(J)},
\]
under which the linear-combination map for \(v\) becomes
\[
(a,b)\longmapsto T_I(a)+T_J(b),
\]
where \(T_I,T_J\) are the linear-combination maps of the two restrictions.

Then organize the argument around the standard injectivity criterion for this sum map: it is injective exactly when \(T_I\) and \(T_J\) are injective and their images intersect trivially. Translate these three conditions back as linear independence of each restriction and disjointness of their spans, using \(\operatorname{range}(T_I)=\operatorname{span}(v|_I)\) and similarly for \(J\). The key mechanism is thus the direct-sum decomposition of finitely supported relations.
